title: fix: make Yaml.__eq__ second arg positional-only
description:
This PR makes a small change to the method signature of the `__eq__` method in the `Yaml` class within `yaml12.pyi`, ensuring that the `other` parameter is positional-only.

Also added a wheel guard in `CI.yml` for the macOS PyPy test step (it was missing the "no wheel found" guard that the Linux job already  has).

title: fix: add the benchmarks section to the GD-based site
description: This PR reintroduces the Benchmarks page, making it part of a dedicated "Benchmarks" section. There's no way to preview what this will look like here in the PR but, from building locally, here's an excerpt of that page: The site will also generally look a bit different than before since several versions of Great Docs were released since the last build of the `yaml12` site.

title: Add Great Docs site (including workflow file)
description:
This PR provides the initial configuration of the Great Docs site (as `great-docs.yml`) and sets up a minimal `docs` directory. The User Guide materials were placed in `user_guide` and the `benchmarks.qmd` file was placed in the `benchmarks` dir for the time being (will re-integrate into the docs once the docs are building correctly).

The workflow file `docs.yml` should build the documentation as it currently successfully does on https://github.com/rich-iannone/great-docs.

title: docs: migrate mkdocs site to great-docs
description: Replace MkDocs with great-docs/Quarto, move narrative docs to user_guide/, enable executable {python} chunks via QUARTO_PYTHON, and add docs workflow.

title: ci: single-workflow abi3 + PyPy wheels
description:
This PR keeps the default `maturin generate-ci` shape, but extends it to ship PyPy wheels from the same workflow and aligns the Rust build with `maturin init` defaults.

- Rust build config: `cdylib` only (drop `rlib` + `build.rs`), bump to `pyo3 0.27.2`, and keep CPython wheels as `cp310-abi3` via `pyo3/abi3-py310` (no `[tool.maturin]` feature flags).
- Tests: move the old `tests/basic.rs` integration coverage into `src/lib.rs` unit tests so `cargo test` works without linking against libpython.
- CI: a single `.github/workflows/CI.yml` builds/uploads CPython (abi3) wheels and PyPy wheels (macOS arm64 + Windows x64; Linux x86_64 when a `pp*.whl` is produced) and runs `tests_py` against both.
- Emscripten: add a best-effort `wasm32-unknown-emscripten` wheel build job that uploads a `wasm-wheels` artifact (not uploaded to PyPI).

title: yaml12: native Yaml wrapper + tag/formatting polish
description:
This PR keeps the public Python API (`parse_yaml`, `read_yaml`, `format_yaml`, `write_yaml`) intact, but refactors the tagged-wrapper type and tightens tag + formatting behavior/perf.

- `yaml12.Yaml` is now a native Rust `pyclass`: immutable `.value`/`.tag`, hashable, picklable, and proxies mapping/sequence operations when wrapping collections/keys.
- Tag semantics are now explicit: non-core tags are preserved as `Yaml`; core scalar tags (`!!str`/`!!int`/`!!float`/`!!bool`/`!!null`/`!!seq`/`!!map`) normalize to plain Python values, while informative core tags (e.g. `!!timestamp`, `!!binary`) stay tagged unless handled.
- Handler normalization: handler keys can be `!foo`/`foo`, verbatim `!<...>` and `%TAG`-expanded URIs, and core shorthand `!!timestamp`/`!!binary`.
- `parse_yaml` accepts `str` or any iterable of `str` chunks (concatenated exactly; no implicit newline insertion).
- `format_yaml` round-trips float edge cases (`1.0`, `-0.0`, `inf`, `-inf`, `nan`), drops core scalar tags on emit, and rejects `bytes`/`bytearray` inputs (use `str` + tags/handlers for binary data).
- Unhashable mapping keys are wrapped in `Yaml` and compare/hash structurally (including mapping insertion order) so they can round-trip safely.
- Performance: `format_yaml` borrows Python `str` values zero-copy during conversion, and handler lookups are cached.
- Docs/typing/tests updated to match the extension runtime; packaging/docs now use the PyPI name `py-yaml12`.

title: io: enforce text writers; simplify stubs
description:
This PR tightens `write_yaml`'s writer contract and simplifies typing support.

## Changes
- `write_yaml`: require a text writer that accepts `str` via `.write(str)`; reject binary writers with a clear error.
- `write_yaml`: support partial writes by looping on the `.write()` return value.
- `sys.stdout` writes: use the same partial-write handling with a safe fallback if `sys.stdout` is malformed.
- Typing: simplify `yaml12.pyi` by dropping Python 3.14 `io.Reader/io.Writer` special-casing; use small Protocols instead.
- Typing: provide precise recursive YAML return types (`_YamlOutput`) when `handlers=None`; keep the `handlers` path as `Any`.
- Tests/docs: update docs and extend Python tests (including mypy/pyright checks and custom reader/writer examples).

title: Add type stubs and CI typing checks
description:
Changes

- Add `yaml12.pyi` for the public Python API.
- Add a Python type-check test to validate the stubs.
- Update CI to run wheel tests and typing checks (and adjust workflow publishing/configuration).

title: parse_yaml: accept iterables and treat chunks as-is
description:
Changes

- Allow `parse_yaml()` to accept iterables of strings (in addition to `str`).
- Treat iterable items as raw text chunks concatenated as-is (no implicit `"\n"` joining).
- Improve error messages for non-string items in sequences/iterables.

title: write_yaml: honor sys.stdout when path is None
description:
Changes

- When `path` is `None`, `write_yaml()` writes to Python `sys.stdout` (so `contextlib.redirect_stdout` works) and falls back to the real stdout when `sys.stdout` is missing or malformed.

title: Release GIL for large YAML parse/emit and file I/O; simplify read_yaml
description:
Changes

- Release the GIL for large YAML parsing and emitting using `py.allow_threads()` (thresholded).
- Release the GIL for filesystem read/write in `read_yaml()`/`write_yaml()` using `py.allow_threads()`.
- Simplify `read_yaml()` by reading the full input once (paths, path-like objects, or `.read()` returning `str`/`bytes`) and parsing from a single buffer.

title: docs: polish Python docs and switch links to posit-dev
description:
- Expand README with file I/O, handlers, and tagged/unhashable key examples; clarify YAML 1.2/JSON relationship and Yaml wrapper role.
- Rework “YAML in 2 Minutes” and advanced tags guides to match R vignette pacing and prose→example flow.
- Add small Yaml round‑trip snippet to overview.
- Update docs site/repo metadata and citation URLs from t‑kalinowski to posit‑dev.

title: Update YAML emission and file APIs
description:
## Summary

This brings the Python package's YAML formatting and file APIs in line with behavior already implemented in r-yaml12. It adds readable, lossless string emission while preserving exact round trips, and exposes the corresponding formatting and file-writing options.

## User-facing changes

- `format_yaml()` and `write_yaml()` now accept an integer `width`, defaulting to 80; `None` disables wrapping.
- Long and paragraph-shaped strings use lossless folded or literal block styles. YAML 1.2-safe strings avoid unnecessary quotes, oversized core-integer strings remain quoted, and overlong mapping keys use explicit syntax.
- Non-finite floats use the canonical `.Inf`, `-.Inf`, and `.NaN` spellings.
- `write_yaml()` supports appending complete documents.
- `read_yaml()` and `write_yaml()` expand paths beginning with `~` using `os.path.expanduser()`.
- Public stubs, README examples, and `NEWS.md` document the updated API.

## Internal changes

The package now uses a local emitter derived from Saphyr so wrapping, quoting, block-scalar, and simple-key behavior can be controlled without changing dependency pins. Existing borrowed-string conversion and GIL-release paths remain in place.

title: Replace stale docs deployment with artifact preview
description:
## Summary

Replace the start-only PR docs deployment with an artifact-based preview flow. The old workflow created a `pr-<number>` deployment but never hosted the site or completed the deployment, leaving GitHub showing it as in progress.

## User-facing changes

- Keep each PR's rendered documentation available as the `docs-html` artifact.
- Add an Actions notice with a command that downloads the exact artifact and serves it locally.
- Install Great Docs from its published package in the local setup instructions.

## Internal changes

- Remove `bobheadxi/deployments`, the deployment permission, and the unused pull-request permission.
- Include hidden generated site files in both the saved documentation artifact and the Pages artifact.
- Point the Great Docs configuration comment at the canonical Posit documentation.
- Leave main-branch GitHub Pages publishing unchanged.

## Notes

Great Docs 0.16.0 is the current published release and does not yet contain its newer remote-preview commands. This uses `gh run download` instead of pulling unreleased Great Docs code into CI.

title: Update project dependencies
description:
## Summary

Update py-yaml12's dependency baseline in one pass, bringing the shared Saphyr revision in line with r-yaml12 and keeping the build and release workflows current.

## User-facing changes

- Pick up the Saphyr 0.0.11 parser fixes while preserving the existing public Python API and output contracts.
- Add no new runtime Python dependencies.

## Internal changes

- Update PyO3 from 0.27.2 to 0.29.2 and the Maturin build baseline from 1.9 to 1.14.
- Declare Rust 1.83 as the minimum supported toolchain required by the new PyO3 release.
- Refresh the complete Cargo lockfile, including Saphyr and saphyr-parser from 0.0.6 to 0.0.11 at the same revision used by r-yaml12.
- Update the GitHub Actions dependencies used for builds, artifacts, attestations, Pages, and Emscripten setup.
